title: Gemini 4 Carbon is the new #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5
content:
October 28, 2026
Gemini 4 Carbon is the new #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5
See model page
Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon is the new #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, and second only to Claude Opus 5.5 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index
Gemini 4 Carbon scores 59 on Intelligence Index v5, driven by leading performance in complex reasoning, knowledge, and scientific tasks. It also has large gains in coding and knowledge work, particularly when compared to other Gemini models, but it is not leading in all these areas.
As with launch of Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 4 Carbon is being rolled out to selected users and is not yet publicly available. Google is offering a 50% launch discount, with no confirmed end date. All our charts and figures use standard pricing for both Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon.
Key results for Gemini 4 Carbon with high reasoning:
➤ Gemini 4 Carbon leads the Intelligence Index v5, with the #1 score in 4 of the 9 Index evaluations: HLE-Diamond, Terminal-Bench-Science, AA-Omniscience, AutomationBench-AA. Carbon makes substantial gains elsewhere but is not leading in coding and knowledge work
➤ Behind only Claude Opus 5.5 on coding agents: With Antigravity CLI, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) scores 59 only 3 points behind Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 62) on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index. Carbon ranks second on both Terminal-Bench 4.0 (64%) and FrontierCode v1.1 (51%), behind Claude Opus 5.5 (max) at 56%. Google has historically underperformed in this area and so this improvement stands out.
➤ Improved agentic knowledge work, but not yet leading: On AA-Briefcase, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) scores 1609 Elo, a 126-point improvement over Gemini 4 Argon (high, 1483), but still behind models including Grok 4.7 (xhigh, 1638), Muse Wonder (max, 1659) and Kimi K3.1 Pro (1678). The largest gain comes from Presentation, up 293 Elo to 1598, alongside a 120-point improvement in Analytical Quality to 1671
➤ Lower Cost per Task than Claude Opus 5.5 for comparable overall intelligence: With standard pricing, Gemini 4 Carbon costs $7.76 per Intelligence Index task, ~23% less than Claude Opus 5.5 (max, $10.04) but ~1.2x GPT-6 Astra (max, $6.25). It uses 123k output tokens per task, 29% fewer than Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 173k). At the same $4/$20 standard pricing, its Cost per Task is in line with Gemini 4 Argon ($7.68), while scoring 9 points higher on the Intelligence Index
➤ Leading AA-Omniscience v1.1 score, with low hallucination: Gemini 4 Carbon scores 54 on our recently updated AA-Omniscience v1.1, 6 points ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 48) and 8 points ahead of Gemini 4 Argon (46). Accuracy (% correct) rises 10 points over Argon to 58%, while its hallucination rate rises from 4% to 11%. This is still the second lowest of any model, behind only Argon, compared with 50% for both Claude Opus 5.5 (max) and GPT-6 Astra (max)
Key model details:
➤ Context Window: 1M tokens
➤ Multimodality: Text, image, video, and speech input, with text output
➤ Pricing: $4/$20 per 1M input/output tokens, the same as Gemini 4 Argon’s standard pricing, with a 50% discount. Cached input tokens receive a 95% discount ($0.20 per 1M at standard pricing)

report.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon takes #1 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 with a score of 59, but remains second to Claude Opus 5.5 on coding agents.
report.background: Artificial Analysis published the Intelligence Index v5 on October 27, 2026, adding two new benchmarks and upgrading three, with most of the index now built on private datasets to reduce contamination and overfitting to public test sets. That makes a top ranking less about benchmark gaming and more about general capability. Carbon arrives shortly after Gemini 4 Argon and is Google's attempt to convert its strength in knowledge and scientific reasoning into a credible agentic story. The competitive field has widened well beyond the Google-Anthropic-OpenAI trio: Claude Opus 5.5 leads coding agents, GPT-6 Astra undercuts on cost per task, xAI's Grok 4.7 and Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro lead agentic knowledge work, and a model called Muse Wonder sits near the top of that category too. Google is also shipping Carbon as a staged, invite-only rollout with a 50% launch discount and no confirmed end date, echoing how Argon was released and leaving standard pricing as the basis for all comparisons.
key_points: Gemini 4 Carbon scores 59 on Intelligence Index v5 and ranks first in 4 of the 9 constituent evaluations: HLE-Diamond, Terminal-Bench-Science, AA-Omniscience and AutomationBench-AA. Its edge is concentrated in complex reasoning, scientific work and factual knowledge rather than across the board, and it trails the leaders in coding and knowledge-work categories.

On coding agents, Carbon paired with Antigravity CLI scores 59 on the Coding Agent Index, just 3 points behind Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 at 62. It places second on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (64%) and FrontierCode v1.1 (51%), behind Opus 5.5's 56% on the latter. Given Google's historical weakness here, closing to within a few points is the headline improvement.

Agentic knowledge work improved a lot but still isn't best-in-class. Carbon reaches 1609 Elo on AA-Briefcase, a 126-point gain over Gemini 4 Argon, but sits behind Grok 4.7 (1638), Muse Wonder (1659) and Kimi K3.1 Pro (1678). Presentation tasks jumped 293 Elo to 1598, with Analytical Quality up 120 points to 1671.

Cost efficiency is competitive but not dominant. At standard pricing Carbon costs about $7.76 per Intelligence Index task, roughly 23% less than Claude Opus 5.5 at $10.04, but about 1.2x GPT-6 Astra at $6.25. It burns 123k output tokens per task, 29% fewer than Opus 5.5, and delivers 9 more index points than Argon at identical $4/$20 pricing.

Factual reliability is a genuine strength. Carbon scores 54 on AA-Omniscience v1.1, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (48) and Argon (46), with accuracy up 10 points to 58%. Its hallucination rate rose from 4% to 11%, still the second lowest measured, against 50% for both Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. The model offers a 1M-token context window and accepts text, image, video and speech input.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the result narrows the gap between Google and Anthropic on agentic coding, the segment where enterprise spend is concentrating, and reinforces a shift in how models are judged: cost per completed task and hallucination rate now matter as much as raw index scores. Index v5's private-dataset majority raises the bar for credible claims. For developers, Carbon's 1M-token context, native video and speech input, and 95% cached-input discount make it attractive for long-document and multimodal pipelines, but the invite-only rollout and undated discount mean production planning should assume list pricing and a fallback provider. For regular users, the practical win is more reliable factual answers and stronger scientific reasoning, while agentic knowledge-work tasks such as decks and briefs remain better served by rival models for now.
report.tools: Follow the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 and Coding Agent Index dashboards for live rankings and cost-per-task data. To try Carbon, watch Google AI Studio and the Gemini API, plus Antigravity CLI for agentic coding workflows and context caching for cost control. For side-by-side evaluation, use OpenRouter or LiteLLM to route identical prompts across Gemini, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, and benchmark on your own task set rather than index scores alone.
